cues.en: Now let's say we have a graph like this, and we want to solve the all pairs shortest path problem on
this graph.
So in this case the first step is going to be we need to set destination.
So let's say a is the destination.
Then we need to find out the shortest path from A to B, then A to C, then A to D, then A to E.
Now similarly, in the next iteration we are going to set the source to B, then we are going to find
out the shortest path from B to A, b to D, b to e, and b to c.
Then in the next iteration, the source vertex is going to be the c.
So here we need to find out the shortest path from C to A, then C to D, then C to B, then C to E,
and it continues like this for all other vertices over here.
So each time we are going to set the next vertex as a source, then we are going to find out the destinations
from that source vertex to other vertices.
So as I mentioned before, we can solve this problem using the algorithms that we have used in case
of single source shortest path problem.
So here let's bring the back the map that we had before.

So I put it in the short and the vertices between them is the path between them.
So let's say we want to solve all pairs path problem using Dijkstra's algorithm.
Now we have learned that Dijkstra's algorithm can solve this problem by taking the one source and finding
the shortest path from that source to other vertices.
Now, in this case, if you want to solve all pairs shortest path problem, we are going to run Dijkstra's
algorithm five times because here we have five vertices.
So first we are going to take as a source London.
Now if you want to find out the shortest path from London to any other cities using Dijkstra's algorithm,
the solution is going to be like this.
So from London for example, to Paris.
We need to go to direct, then to Berlin.
We have also direct link.
Now, if you want to go to Barcelona from London, we need to go to Paris.
Then we need to go to Rome.
Then we need to go to Barcelona.
So this is going to be the shortest path.
Now if we take as a source vertex city of Paris, in this case, the solution is going to be like this.
Now, in the next step we are going to take as a source Vertex Berlin.
Then the solution is going to be like this.
So for example from Berlin, we don't have direct route to London.
So to be able to go that we need to go to Barcelona, then Paris, then London.
So as you can see, the path is changed.
Now in the next step we are going to take Rome as a source vertex.
Then we are going to find out the destination.
Then in the last step we are going to take Barcelona as a source vertex.
Then we are going to find out the shortest path from Barcelona to any other cities.
Now, as you can see here, we have to run the Dijkstra's algorithm five times.
And similarly we can use the Bellman-ford or BFS algorithm.
All pairs shortest path problem using the same logic.
Now, if we run this algorithm five times, it's really time consuming.
But running these algorithms five times for one problem is not efficient.
So that's why we have another algorithm which is going to solve the all pairs shortest path problem.
So the algorithm called Floyd-warshall algorithm.
Now in the next section we are going to learn about Floyd-warshall algorithm.
